excerpt: UpKeep is maintenance management (CMMS) software for work orders, preventive maintenance and assets, with plans from $24 per user a month. Pricing, funding and alternatives.
content:
UpKeep is a computerised maintenance management system (CMMS): software that maintenance and facilities teams use to create and track work orders, schedule preventive maintenance, manage assets, parts and inventory, and report on downtime. It was built mobile-first so technicians can work from a phone on the shop floor, and it has added safety, training and an AI assistant called Nova. Its website now describes it as an AI-powered maintenance platform.

UpKeep is based in Los Angeles. Y Combinator's directory says it was founded in 2016 and went through YC in winter 2017. TechCrunch reported that founder Ryan Chan had worked at Trisep, a chemical manufacturer, where maintenance was still handled on paper because the plant's software only ran on desktop computers. In May 2020 UpKeep announced a $36 million Series B led by Insight Partners, with Emergence Capital, Battery Ventures, Y Combinator, Mucker Capital and FundersClub taking part; Insight said at the time that more than 2,000 paying businesses and 400,000 users were on the app.

UpKeep publishes its prices. The Essential plan costs $24 per user a month and Premium $55 per user a month; Professional and Enterprise are quoted. Each plan includes a monthly allowance of Nova AI credits, and paid setup and training packages are sold separately. UpKeep competes with MaintainX, Fiix and Limble, and suits teams moving off paper or spreadsheets as much as larger multi-site operations.

We have not used UpKeep for this page. It brings together UpKeep's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
